title: ESPN to Hike Prices of Streaming Plans Next Month
description:
ESPN is ratcheting up the price of its streaming services — just in time for the busy fall sports season.

	Effective Sept. 17, the Disney-owned spo
body:
ESPN is ratcheting up the price of its streaming services — just in time for the busy fall sports season.

	Effective Sept. 17, the Disney-owned sports giant is increasing the monthly and annual pricing for both ESPN Unlimited and the scaled-down ESPN Select tier.

	The price of ESPN Unlimited is increasing from $29.99 to $31.99/month. The cost of the annual ESPN Unlimited plan is rising from $299.99 to $319.99/year. In addition to everything on the ESPN and ESPN2 linear networks, the stand-alone sports package includes ESPNU, ESPNews, ESPN Deportes, SECN, SECN+, ACCN, and ACCNX plus thousands of additional live sporting events per year.
	

	All told, ESPN Unlimited offers more than 47,000 live events each year, including every major sport and championship ESPN presents. The streaming service also recently integrated NFL Network and CW Sports on the ESPN App, and includes features like the personalized “SportsCenter For You”; Verts vertical video; and StreamCenter, a synchronized two-screen experience connecting mobile and connected TV devices.


	ESPN Select is going from $12.99 to $13.99/month, while the annual plan is increasing from $129.99 to $139.99/year. ESPN Select provides some 32,000 live events annually but does not include access to the ESPN linear networks.

	In an Aug. 20 memo to ESPN staffers reviewed by Variety, chairman Jimmy Pitaro praised the team that launched the stand-alone streaming service a year ago.

	Disney has not disclosed how many subscribers have signed up for the ESPN streaming plans. 

	“From the beginning, we set out to provide sports fans with optionality and a new way to connect with ESPN. Early on, we have delivered,” Pitaro wrote. “To everyone across ESPN and Disney who continues to work tirelessly to build this platform — thank you. While we’re still in the early innings of our direct-to-consumer journey, one year after the launch of ESPN DTC, we move forward with absolute confidence in where we are headed.”
	

	“We’re heading into the fall in an exceptionally strong position,” Pitaro wrote in the memo. “The NFL preseason has begun, and we are truly excited about the entire season leading to our first Super Bowl. College football will also kick off soon, a new LaLiga season is already underway, U.S. Open tennis begins this weekend, and so much more lies ahead. Our rights portfolio has never been stronger, and we have strong momentum.”

	According to Pitaro, “maximizing access” the ESPN streaming services has been a priority, “and that focus has led to meaningful progress this year. In fact, subscribers across nearly every major pay TV provider — including recent additions Comcast Xfinity and YouTube TV — can unlock the full ESPN Unlimited tier experience on the ESPN App at no additional cost. We are also focused on supporting Disney+ by unlocking additional content for its subscribers, in service of our One Disney initiative.”

schema.headline: ESPN to Hike Prices of Streaming Plans Next Month

title: John Leguizamo, Inde Navarrette and James Ortiz Among Latino and Hispanic Stars Set for Honors at Critics Choice Celebración Ceremony
description: Veteran actor John Leguizamo, breakouts James Ortiz and Inde Navarrette and more Latino Hollywood talents are among the Critics Choice Association’s
body:
Veteran actor John Leguizamo, breakouts James Ortiz and Inde Navarrette and more Latino Hollywood talents are among the Critics Choice Association’s slate of honorees for the newly titled Celebración of Cinema & Television (formerly called Celebration of Latino Cinema and Television), now in its sixth year, that recognizes and spotlights Latino and Hispanic artistry both on-screen and off. The ceremony takes place Oct. 2 in Beverly Hills.
	

	Leading the class is John Leguizamo, who will receive the Career Achievement Award. The Emmy winner, Special Tony Award recipient and four-time Tony nominee is being feted for a run spanning more than four decades and, most recently, his turn in Universal Pictures’ “The Odyssey,” which the CCA notes posted the biggest live-action opening weekend of the year and has crossed $1 billion globally within three weeks of release. His other notable film and TV credits include “Carlito’s Way” (1993), “Moulin Rouge!” (2001) and the miniseries “When They See Us.”


	Inde Navarrette earns the Breakthrough Actress Award (Film) for Focus Features’ “Obsession,” the box-office phenomenon that has grossed more than $488 million worldwide to become the highest-grossing film in the studio’s history. Laysla De Oliveira rounds out the breakthrough honors with the Breakthrough Actress Award (Series) for Paramount+’s “Lioness,” appearing across all three seasons of Taylor Sheridan’s espionage thriller opposite Zoe Saldaña, who received the Groundbreaker Award from the CCA in 2024 for “Emilia Pérez,” for which she won the Oscar for supporting actress.
	

	James Ortiz will collect the Innovator Award for Amazon MGM’s “Project Hail Mary.” The Broadway puppeteer, whose design work includes the Tony-nominated “The Skin of Our Teeth,” performs, voices and operates the alien Rocky opposite co-star Ryan Gosling in the space-set blockbuster, a turn that has entered this year’s supporting actor Oscar conversation.

	Judy Reyes will take the Trailblazer Award for her work on ABC’s “High Potential,” where she plays Lt. Selena Soto opposite Kaitlin Olson on the crime procedural that became one of the network’s top-rated series in its debut season and its most-watched new series in six years. Reyes also returned this year to the “Scrubs” role she played across more than nine seasons, reprising the character for the comedy’s ABC revival.

	Oscar Núñez will be honored with the Vanguard Award for Peacock’s comedy “The Paper.” The Emmy and SAG Award winner, who originated Oscar Martinez on “The Office,” reprises the character in the new mockumentary, which was renewed for a second season shortly after its premiere.

	Completing the on-screen honorees, Aimee Carrero will receive the Supporting Actress Award (Series) for Apple TV’s “Your Friends & Neighbors,” the dark dramedy whose ensemble helped land it a Primetime Emmy nomination for outstanding drama series for the recent second season, becoming the first drama in history to land a sole nom only in the top series race.

	Elsewhere on the slate, the CCA turns to the storytellers working behind the camera.

	Rodrigo Teixeira lands the Producer Award for Neon’s thriller “Paper Tiger,” his fourth collaboration with director James Gray that premiered at the Cannes Film Festival. The Oscar-nominated producer’s RT Features production banner is behind films like Luca Guadagnino’s “Call Me by Your Name,” which earned four Academy Award nominations including best picture, winning adapted screenplay for James Ivory, and Walter Salles’ “I’m Still Here,” which made history as the first Brazilian Portuguese-language film nominated for best picture and won the Oscar for best international feature.

	Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, the Spanish duo also known as Los Javis, take the Director Award for Netflix’s “La Bola Negra.” The pair behind “Paquita Salas” and the Rose d’Or-winning “La Mesías” claimed the directors’ prize at this year’s Cannes Film Festival for the multigenerational drama, which draws on an unfinished work by Federico García Lorca and stars Penélope Cruz and Glenn Close.
	

	The Celebración also leans into breakout talent. Beth de Araújo receives the Breakthrough Director Award for Sumerian Pictures’ “Josephine,” which made her a rare double winner at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, taking both the Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award. The film, starring Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan, drew an emotional response at the festival, where the Brazilian-American filmmaker used her moment to honor sexual assault survivors.

	“To honor this remarkable class of Latino and Hispanic artists is nothing short of a gift, especially during a time that has been difficult for our communities,” says Clayton Davis, Variety’s chief awards editor and a CCA member and co-programmer of the Celebración. “Latino and Hispanic storytellers keep creating from a place of joy and defiance, turning our histories and culture into art that moves the culture forward. Their work builds a larger, more inclusive tent for everyone to be invited to join.”

	Davis will serve as the writer for the ceremony, and host the celebration alongside Amanda Salas, fellow CCA member and entertainment anchor and reporter on Good Day LA. Javier Infante, Madelyn Hammond and Ella Carlson of Hammond Infante Productions produce the program. Milagro Tequila has signed on as the official spirit sponsor, with LatiNation Media co-hosting the official after-party.

	The Celebración of Cinema and Television is part of the CCA’s slate of events recognizing historically underrepresented communities, which also includes celebrations of Black, AAPI and LGBTQ+ cinema and television.

	The full list of honorees is below.


Career Achievement Award: John Leguizamo, “The Odyssey” (Universal Pictures)
Trailblazer Award: Judy Reyes, “High Potential” (ABC)
Vanguard Award: Oscar Núñez, “The Paper” (Peacock)
Producer Award: Rodrigo Teixeira, “Paper Tiger” (Neon)
Director Award: Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, “La Bola Negra” (Netflix)
Innovator Award: James Ortiz, “Project Hail Mary” (Amazon MGM Studios)
Supporting Actress Award, Series: Aimee Carrero, “Your Friends & Neighbors” (Apple TV)
Breakthrough Director Award: Beth de Araújo, “Josephine” (Sumerian Pictures)
Breakthrough Actress Award, Film: Inde Navarrette, “Obsession” (Focus Features)
Breakthrough Actress Award, Series: Laysla De Oliveira, “Lioness” (Paramount+)

schema.headline: John Leguizamo, Inde Navarrette and James Ortiz Among Latino and Hispanic Stars Set for Honors at Critics Choice Celebración Ceremony

title: WildBrain Acquires ‘Kid Safe’ Generative-AI Platform Personality AI in Deal Worth up to $69 Million
description: WildBrain, the Canadian children’s media company with the rights to titles such as “Yo Gabba Gabba!” and the “Teletubbies,” has purchased the child-
body:
WildBrain, the Canadian children’s media company with the rights to titles such as “Yo Gabba Gabba!” and the “Teletubbies,” has purchased the child-focused generative AI startup Personality AI in a cash-and-stock deal worth up to $69 million in a bid to marry the company’s intellectual property with the startup’s conversational products.

	Personality AI touts its conversational character AIs as child-safe, working with a mixture of AI engineers, child development experts and entertainment producers to develop AI models based on licensed child characters that implement safeguards as children engage with them while not retaining child data. Amazon selected Personality AI last year to develop a platform on its kids-focused subscription service Amazon Kids+, leading to a “Peppa Pig”-based generative product for children to engage with the fictional British icon. 
	

	The company is also part of the Federal Trade Commission-backed COPPA Safe Harbor Program, one of the leading independent oversight programs related to federal child privacy protections. WildBrain hopes the acquisition will boost the revenue opportunities for its array of IP, including “Degrassi” and “Strawberry Shortcake.”


	“Personality AI enables more continuous interaction between fans and brands, strengthening our ability to deliver end-to-end franchise solutions to partners,” WildBrain CEO and president Josh Sceherba said in a statement. “This highly complementary acquisition positions us and Personality AI as a more integrated partner to IP owners globally through our in-house licensing agency, WildBrain CPLG, while helping support the continued growth of both our owned and partner brands.”
	

	Wildbrain paid roughly $11 million in cash along with 1 million shares. Shareholders will also receive $2 million worth of WildBrain shares (up to 1 million shares) in additional consideration on the first anniversary of closing, with the remaining balance paid in cash. The deal also includes up to $56 million in performance-based cash consideration based on Personality AI’s revenue performance between 2027 and 2029. Personality CEO John Goscha will join WildBrain as the executive vice president for Personality AI and will report to Scherba.

	“I’m thrilled to be joining forces with WildBrain, a clear leader in family entertainment,” Goscha said in a statement. “At Personality AI, we share WildBrain’s commitment to children’s wellbeing, which is why we employ rigorous safety standards to ensure appropriate, authentic and trustworthy content and experiences for kids, parents and IP owners alike.”

schema.headline: WildBrain Acquires ‘Kid Safe’ Generative-AI Platform Personality AI in Deal Worth up to $69 Million

title: ‘Small Things’ Review: Zvonimir Jurić’s Island-Set Chamber Drama Unfolds a Quietly Devastating Family Reunion
description: In the opening of “Small Things,” Zvonimir Jurić’s elegant and understated chamber drama, the giggling grandchildren of an elder patriarch (Bosnian
body:
In the opening of “Small Things,” Zvonimir Jurić’s elegant and understated chamber drama, the giggling grandchildren of an elder patriarch (Bosnian film and theater veteran Izudin Bajrović) show their charmingly clueless pops how to operate a smartphone. Later that night, along with the kids’ mother Irena (Ivana Roščić) and aunt Anica (Marija Skaričić), the crew plays a round of “Who Am I?” where the cards read both former Yugoslavian songstresses and western celebrities like Paris Hilton and Lady Gaga. From here, modernity’s encroachment weaves through this family reunion in less obvious and more existentially crippling ways, which the Croatian writer-director — making his return in competition at Sarajevo 12 years after his last feature “The Reaper” — unfolds with a whispered, windswept melancholy suited to the somber Adriatic island setting. 
	

	The sale of their father’s orchard and the ensuing inheritance negotiations have brought sisters Anica and Irena, who live on the Croatian mainland, back to their rustic family home. With no score, the film’s vivid sound design of billowing foliage, creaky doors and floorboards, creates an austere ambience that softens with quiet feeling as the contours of the family’s troubles are gradually filled out. During visits to their mother’s clifftop grave and humble corner shops where locals continue to buy on account, we discover that Anica’s partner died recently of cancer, while pregnant Irena’s coming child is a kind of last-ditch effort to save her crumbling marriage. 


	Meanwhile, their catatonic brother Ivan (Juraj Lerotić) emerges from his groundfloor room only to go squidfishing, or to prepare himself a bowl of miserably insubstantial instant soup that he takes immediately back down to his chambers. Anyone who’s seen Lerotić’s directorial debut, “Safe Place,” which won Sarajevo’s top prize in 2022 as well as a handful of awards out of Locarno, will inevitably filter his performance in “Small Things” through the lens of that film’s aching exploration of suicide. 
	

	Though Lerotić startles as Ivan in his gloomy, gaunt vacancy, casting a fearsome cloud of mortality over each frame he enters, the script by Jurić and Jurica Pavičić (who wrote the short story the film is adapted from) keeps the ensemble drama carefully balanced by anchoring big sister Anica’s point-of-view. Childless and alone yet stable relative to her siblings, Anica assumes the head of the family and takes it upon herself to pull Ivan out of his slump, though her compassion chills when money-strapped Irena makes a bid for Ivan’s chunk of the inheritance. In step with the film’s moody sense of suspended time, dramatic faceoffs play out with restraint, through gestures and glances that signal complicated interpersonal histories — for instance, a mere icy glance from the judgmental Anica makes Irena collapse into tears. 

	Working with “Safe Place” cinematographer Marko Brdar, Jurić extends this emotional reserve to the film’s mostly static images and natural lighting, which lends the family’s weathered abode a sort of dusky inertia. Ivan’s room feels practically airless, his face obscured in shadows, or captured in hazy side profiles, as Anica’s bright, concerned gaze holds the frame’s focus. The film’s unrushed, small-scale beauty might be imperceptible to a more plot-hungry viewer, though slow-cinema oriented distributors might do well to take a chance on this Croatian gem. Likewise, the film rewards patience with an agonizingly tender culminating shot — a reminder that some things must change while others linger in the amber of childhood.

schema.headline: ‘Small Things’ Review: Zvonimir Jurić’s Island-Set Chamber Drama Unfolds a Quietly Devastating Family Reunion

title: Orlando Bloom to Be Honored During Venice Film Festival With Filming Italy Award
description: Orlando Bloom, who will be attending the Venice Film Festival as part of the cast of Warner Herzog’s competition title “Bucking Fastard,” is set to
body:
Orlando Bloom, who will be attending the Venice Film Festival as part of the cast of Warner Herzog’s competition title “Bucking Fastard,” is set to be feted on the Lido with the Filming Italy International Award from Filming Italy — Los Angeles, the event that bridges Italy and Hollywood.

	Bloom will receive the award, which is not connected to the Venice Film Festival, on Sept. 6.


	“It is a great honor for us to welcome Orlando Bloom to the latest edition of the Filming Italy Venice Award,” said marketing guru and longtime Italian industry promoter Tiziana Rocca in a statement. Rocca, who heads Filming Italy and also leads the Taormina Film Festival, praised Bloom as “an actor of extraordinary charisma, capable of captivating audiences around the world with his elegance, talent and versatility,” noting that he has “achieved international fame thanks to his participation in two of the greatest film sagas of all time: ‘The Lord of the Rings’ and ‘Pirates of the Caribbean.'”
	

	Bloom recently appeared in Sean Ellis’ boxing thriller “The Cut,” which he also produced through his production company Amazing Owl, and crime comedy caper “Deep Cover,” a Prime Video U.K. Original movie directed by Tom Kingsley.


	In “Bucking Fastard,” Bloom plays Gareth Mulroney, the lover of inseparable, synchronized twin sisters Jean and Joan Holbrooke (played by real-life sisters Kate and Rooney Mara) whom they obsess over after becoming tabloid sensations, according to the film’s synopsis.

	The upcoming 83rd Venice Film Festival runs from Sept. 2 to 12.

schema.headline: Orlando Bloom to Be Honored During Venice Film Festival With Filming Italy Award

title: Reggie Watts’ Theme Song Axed From ‘Comedy Bang Bang’ Podcast After Report Alleging ‘Reckless’ Drug Use in Relationships
description: Reggie Watts’ “Comedy Bang Bang” theme song was cut from Monday’s episode of the popular podcast following a Rolling Stone report that alleged the c
body:
Reggie Watts’ “Comedy Bang Bang” theme song was cut from Monday’s episode of the popular podcast following a Rolling Stone report that alleged the comedian and musician has exhibited “reckless and selfish” behavior regarding drugs in his past relationships.

	The story, which was published on Thursday, alleges that Watts’ late ex-girlfriend, Katherine McCollough, developed a ketamine addiction while dating him (Watts has been a longtime advocate for the drug). Their relationship ended in October 2025 after McCollough experienced a drug-induced manic episode that summer, and in March of this year, McCollough traveled to Peru to take her own life. In a statement to Rolling Stone, Watts’ attorney Andrew Brettler called the claims “dangerously false” and said it was a “preconceived narrative” to suggest that he was responsible for her suicide.
	

	Watts — known for starring in the TV version of “Comedy Bang Bang” from 2012 to 2016 before becoming the bandleader for James Corden’s “Late Late Show” — penned the theme song for the Scott Aukerman-hosted podcast, which began airing as a radio show in 2009. The song was played before last week’s episode on Aug. 17, but is not present in Monday’s installment featuring Fred Armisen and Carrie Brownstein of “Portlandia” fame.


	Representatives for Watts, “Comedy Bang Bang” and Aukerman did not immediately respond to Variety‘s request for comment.

	In addition to McCollough’s story, the Rolling Stone report contains claims from five women who previously dated Watts and allege a pattern of “reckless and selfish” behavior regarding drugs in their relationships. Two women alleged that their relationships with Watts were “emotionally and psychologically abusive.”
	

	McCollough’s family and friends told Rolling Stone that her drug consumption “drastically increased” while dating Watts and became a “central” part of their relationship. In his statement, Watts’ lawyer said that McCollough was already an “experienced” drug user and did not need “any so-called ‘encouragement,'” and added that any suggestion of Watts being an “abusive” boyfriend was false.

	Those close to McCollough “firmly believe that if McCollough had never met Watts, had he not pushed his extreme views on psychedelics and substances on her and had McCollough not adopted those views, that she’d still be alive today,” the Rolling Stone report states.

schema.headline: Reggie Watts’ Theme Song Axed From ‘Comedy Bang Bang’ Podcast After Report Alleging ‘Reckless’ Drug Use in Relationships

title: ‘The Gentlemen’ Officially Renewed for Season 3 as First Season 2 Trailer Drops: ‘I’m Looking Forward to Pushing the Boundaries Further,’ Guy Ritchie Says (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
“The Gentlemen” has officially been greenlit for Season 3, Variety can confirm.

	Guy Ritchie’s high-society, high-octane caper starring Theo James
body:
“The Gentlemen” has officially been greenlit for Season 3, Variety can confirm.

	Guy Ritchie’s high-society, high-octane caper starring Theo James and Kaya Scodelario is set to return for a third outing, comprised of eight episodes. Variety understands that while the new season is in pre-production no scripts have yet been finalized, let alone new casting, despite rumors of Meghan Markle joining. The show is due to go into production imminently. 
	

	“The ambition of ‘The Gentlemen’ has accelerated, the world has expanded and the consequences carry weight,” says creator, writer, director and executive producer Guy Ritchie. “A third season felt inevitable, and I’m looking forward to pushing the boundaries of it further.”


	Ritchie will also be returning to direct Season 3, which he co-writes with Matthew Read.

	The news of the third season comes amid a host of returning season orders for some of Netflix’s top U.K. shows including “Black Mirror” Season 8, “Legends” Season 2 and “Being Gordon Ramsay” Season 2. Other highly anticipated Netflix U.K. dramas returning for a second season are “Supacell,” “Black Doves” and “House of Guinness.”

	The streamer today also released its first full-length trailer for “The Gentlemen” Season 2, ahead of its launch on Sept. 3.



	

					Kaya Scodelario in ‘The Gentlemen’ Season 2 (courtesy of Netflix)
	



	Season 2 will see Eddie Horniman (James) and Susie Glass (Scodelario) grow their business internationally as they take to the lakeside villas of Italy where at least one of their crew finds out he’s bitten off more than he can chew.
	

	Meanwhile Eddie’s rise through the criminal underworld is mirrored by his rise through the British establishment, bringing him into the circle of a new oleaginous aristo played by Hugh Bonneville, who is joining the cast.

	In the trailer, Eddie hints at his growing ambitions, as he tells Geoff of his stately pile: “Four hundred years ago, this estate spread out as far as the eye could see. I want it all back.”

	With American billionaire Stanley Johnston (Giancarlo Esposito) whispering in his hear (“You are destined to rule, forge your own path”) Eddie’s confidence in his ability to play high-stakes games with notorious crime lords soars ever higher — but at what cost?

	Season 2 sees Ray Winstone returning as Glass’s kingpin father Bobby while Harry Goodwins returns as her brawny brother Jack.

	On the Duke’s side, Joely Richardson is back as Eddie’s mother Lady Sabrina, Daniel Ings as disinherited older brother Freddy, Jasmine Blackborow as sister Charly and Vinnie Jones as Geoff, keeper of the grounds – and family secrets.



	

					Hugh Bonneville and Harry Goodwins in ‘The Gentlemen’ Season 2 (courtesy of Netflix)
	



	Also returning for Season 2 are Esposito, Michael Vu, Ruby Sear and Pearce Quigley.

	Joining the cast this season are Benjamin Clementine (“Dune”), Benedetta Porcaroli (“The Leopard”), Amra Mallassi (“Dune: Part Two”), Tyler Conti (“Tell Me Everything”), professional boxer Chris Eubank Jr and “Love Island U.K.” host Maya Jama.

	“The Gentlemen” is produced by Moonage Pictures for Netflix and Miramax TV. Exec producers are Ritchie, Read, Ivan Atkinson, Will Gould, Simon Crawford, Collins and Frith Tiplady for Moonage Pictures alongside Jonathan Glickman and Marc Helwig for Miramax TV,

	Check out the new trailer below:

title: Rosie O’Donnell Should Host Her Own Show on Late-Night TV — and Shatter Comedy’s Greatest Glass Ceiling
description: Late night is in the doldrums. It’s not just that the remaining hosts are taking much of the summer off. But, post-Stephen Colbert on CBS, ABC’s Jim
body:
Late night is in the doldrums. It’s not just that the remaining hosts are taking much of the summer off. But, post-Stephen Colbert on CBS, ABC’s Jimmy Kimmel and NBC’s Jimmy Fallon both feel closer to the end of their respective tenures than the beginning. The whole genre feels ripe for a shake-up — lest it go away entirely.

	Enter Rosie O’Donnell. The comedian and Donald Trump antagonist just spent a week filling in for Jimmy Kimmel, and the results were TV magic. Over four nights, O’Donnell, the 1990s talk show host whose two stints on “The View” both fizzled out, proved that she may yet have another act, and it may be on one of television’s grandest — diminished, but still grandest — stages.
	

	Yes, O’Donnell skewered President Trump, and it, of course, drew attention: O’Donnell is, these days, perhaps best known as an object of Trump’s obsession. (Indeed, the White House issued a statement that O’Donnell “is a nasty woman and a total slob whose brain has been completely destroyed by Trump Derangement Syndrome.”) But her approach to her monologues tended toward reconnecting with the audience over rat-a-tat resistance patter. Combining this impulse for empathetic opening-up with a savage instinct for finding the laugh, O’Donnell proved that, while late night may be growing a bit soft, she arrived at “Kimmel” ready for the spotlight. 


	It’s been almost 40 years since Joan Rivers tried to break into the late-night boys’ club — and got fired by Fox after a single season. O’Donnell’s hiring as a woman at a flagship late-night show would break further ground — but would also bring in someone who totally reveres television and knows how to make it well. A form of TV that seems close to dying could use a jolt of energy, and O’Donnell, with her built-in fanbase and her ability to connect with, and provoke, audiences, might just be late night’s future. 
	

	Sound familiar? That’s because we just saw it play out in fiction. In the universe of “Hacks,” women have been given only paltry chances to claim their piece of late night. Eventually, Jean Smart’s character Deborah Vance, whose comedy alternately undermines and exalts her own image and is rooted in her rock-solid showbiz chops, gets her chance. (Let’s, for now, not worry about the fact that it all blows up in relatively short order.) 

	On “Hacks,” as in our world, late night looks like a glass cliff for women — the field is shrinking, with CBS now out of the game entirely, just in time for a woman to potentially get called up. And yet, O’Donnell didn’t seem to mind, and hit the ground running on “Kimmel.” The female late-night hosts of recent vintage, CBS’ Taylor Tomlinson and NBC’s Lilly Singh, have seemed limited by both buried-in-the-evening time slot and by relatively low name recognition. O’Donnell’s hiring would be a moment that would electrify late night, drawing in an underserved audience of women and gay men and generating reams of press. 

	Shifting from wish-casting O’Donnell into a late-night berth and actually considering what might be possible, there are obvious counterarguments. After early success, O’Donnell has suffered disappointment after disappointment. She left “The View” in 2007 over an incident in which she and co-host Elisabeth Hasselbeck were presented arguing in split-screen, and then returned for another short run, from 2014 to 2015, that was simply unremarkable before she once again quit. In between, she tried an Oprah Winfrey Network talk show and a Sirius radio show. Nothing stuck. 

	But unlike on “The View,” where she was one of several panelists sniping round-robin style, O’Donnell, here, would be in a position that we know suits her — behind a desk, telling jokes. She came into “The View” to blow it up; as regards TV talk, though, we already know she’s a traditionalist. In childhood, O’Donnell was a student of early TV, and she seems to have totally internalized old-school broadcast rhythms. Among them are a total and complete interest in whoever is in front of her. I’ve written before that, in his final months, Colbert seemed to come most alive when his interview subjects got around to praising him, and Kimmel or Fallon’s strengths are not necessarily in interviewing, either. O’Donnell, on the other hand, knew how to steer guests from the digressive Smart to the antsy Richard Gadd toward the funniest and most charming versions of themselves. 
	

	She was coming to the show with the zeal of someone who’s been out of the game too long and eager for her at-bat. The standard monologue nowadays can feel like a laundry list of cracks about Trump’s daily misdeeds. O’Donnell’s curiosity — for all that she’s the President’s bête noire — ranged more widely. She got personal about her family and dating life in a manner I’d never expect a Jimmy to do. And she did so with a sense of real craft, the sort that comes when you’re excited to be somewhere and not just clocking in for season umpteen. 

	But then, O’Donnell is, first, a storyteller, well acquainted by now with fitting the tales she tells within the time between the “Applause” sign lighting up and the first commercial break. The discursive looseness of her posting on social media — where, for instance, she recently disclosed her face-lift — falls away when the camera is on her. When I interviewed her last year, about her guest role on “And Just Like That,” she described to me that, in her newly adopted home of Ireland, the local pharmacist was so kind to her that O’Donnell developed a crush. On her first Kimmel monologue, the story was blown out, underlined, illuminated by a star’s charisma. Of course, it built to the perfect punchline.

	Who knows if she’d get the chance — Kimmel perennially makes noise about wanting to leave, but hasn’t yet — or if she’d want to. (Although the fact of her returning to the U.S. before the end of the Trump presidency, which she once swore she wouldn’t, suggests a bit of fire in the belly.) But one wonders if the industry, not just viewers, shares the sense that the TV landscape is significantly more interesting with O’Donnell in it — and that interest is exactly what late night is lacking. If this is O’Donnell’s moment, it’s not because of who the President is. It’s because of who, over four remarkable nights of old-school television, she reminded us she is.

schema.headline: Rosie O’Donnell Should Host Her Own Show on Late-Night TV — and Shatter Comedy’s Greatest Glass Ceiling

title: ‘Black Mirror’ Season 8 Starts Production as Netflix Renews ‘Being Gordon Ramsay’ and ‘Legends’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
An eighth season of “Black Mirror” is officially in production, Variety can confirm. 

	The show started shooting this summer, although no launch da
body:
An eighth season of “Black Mirror” is officially in production, Variety can confirm. 

	The show started shooting this summer, although no launch date for the new season has been set yet.

	Earlier this year creator Charlie Brooker vowed the dystopian anthology series “will return, and hopefully it’ll be more ‘Black Mirror’ than ever.” He is writing and exec producing the eighth season alongside Bisha K.Ali. Jessica Rhoades, Annabel Jones, Louise Sutton also EP while Mark Kinsella is a co-exec producer on the series, which is licensed by Banijay Rights.
	

	The news comes as Netflix also confirms Season 2 orders for hit Neil Forsyth drama “Legends,” about a group of undercover customers officers, and reality series “Being Gordon Ramsay,” about the iconic chef and his growing family. The streamer also today confirmed “The Gentlemen” is set to return for a third season (Season 2 launched Sept. 3).


	“Being Gordon Ramsay” will return to the streamer next year, with production already underway. “Gordon Ramsay is busier than ever,” the synopsis promises. “With restaurants to run, a 25-year anniversary to mark and a global brand to oversee, Gordon’s schedule is packed to the brim. Alongside the business empire, his family remains his greatest priority.”

	The show is produced by Studio Ramsay Global. Exec producers are Ramsay, Amanda Westwood and Lisa Edwards. Dionne Bromfield directs and produces.

	Meanwhile the new season of “Legends,” comprised of 6 episodes, will go into production next year. “I’m delighted to have the opportunity to tell a new story in the fascinating and unique world that ‘Legends’ offers, and to show just how dangerous, thrilling, and important their work became in the late 1990s,” said Forsyth.
	

	Forsyth exec produces alongside Ben Farrell, Rhiannon Forsyth for Tannadice Pictures, and Richard Bradley for Lion Television. “Legends” is produced by Tannadice Pictures, an Objective Media Group company, in association with Lion Television, both part of Banijay Entertainment.

	“As the story moves further into the 1990s, a changing Britain faces a new drugs threat on a scale never seen before,” reads the Season 2 synopsis. “The team of undercover Custom Officers come together once more to take on new challenges, and new enemies, in a thrilling, worldwide operation.”



	

	



	The streamer previously announced other popular U.K. dramas would also be returning for new outings including second seasons of “Supacell,” “House of Guinness” and “Black Doves.”

	“Supacell” season 2 has just wrapped and is eyeing a 2027 release date, while the new instalment of “Black Doves” will hit screens later this year. “House of Guinness,” comprised of six episodes, is set to go into production in January.

	“It was such a joy to bring the Guinness story to the screen, so I’m beyond thrilled to be continuing the story of one of the world’s greatest dynasties into Season 2,” said creator Steven Knight. “I can’t wait to dive deeper into these characters and their complex relationships as they expand the Guinness empire.”

	In unscripted, audiences can look forward to the return of “Formula 1: Drive to Survive” (Season 9), coming to Netflix next year, “Love is Blind U.K.” (Season 4), which is set to start shooting next month with a new group of hopeful singles and is eyeing a 2027 release date, “At Home with the Furys” (Season 3), which is currently in production and “The Rest is Football” (Season 2), which will return for the 2026/27 Premier League season.

	“Our audiences loved these shows so it is such a delight to bring them back,” says Anne Mensah, Netflix’s VP for U.K. content. “To revisit the Guinness family, cook with the Ramsays, go undercover with the Legends and be At Home With The Furys. A huge thank you to the brilliant producers, actors, writers, directors and crew behind these shows and all of our returners on Netflix — it’s an utter privilege to host these gems.”

schema.headline: ‘Black Mirror’ Season 8 Starts Production as Netflix Renews ‘Being Gordon Ramsay’ and ‘Legends’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Guillermo del Toro, James Gunn, ‘Beyond the Spider-Verse’ Directors Set for Crunchyroll’s Inaugural Anime Future Forum
description: Anime giant Crunchyroll plans to dissect the growing business of anime with its first-ever thought leadership summit to be held as a precursor to Ne
body:
Anime giant Crunchyroll plans to dissect the growing business of anime with its first-ever thought leadership summit to be held as a precursor to New York Comic Con in October.

	The Crunchyroll Anime Future Forum will be held Oct. 7 at New York’s Javits Convention Center, with conference tracks focusing on four key themes: fandom, technology, storytelling and IP protection. 

	Notables set to speak at the event include director Guillermo del Toro, a longtime proponent of anime, director James Gunn, and Bob Persichetti and Justin K. Thompson, directors of Sony Pictures’ upcoming animated sequel “Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse.” Anime influencers including Amber Glenn, Big Sean and Jordan Howlett will also take part.
	

	Top anime studios will also be showcased, including leaders from Toho (Taichi Ueda, film producer and executive officer), MAPPA (Manabu Otsuka, president and CEO) and Sony Music’s Aniplex (Atsuhiro Iwakami, Group CEO, representative director of Sony Music Entertainment (Japan) Inc. and chairman of Aniplex Inc.).


	Sony Corp.’s top leaders will be out in force to support the event. Crunchyroll has been under the Sony Pictures Entertainment umbrella since 2021, when the studio acquired Crunchyroll and merged it with Sony’s existing Funimation unit. The subscription streaming platform has blossomed into Sony’s biggest footprint in streaming and an engine of distinctive content for the company. Crunchyroll partnered with Sony Pictures for the theatrical rollout of 2025’s “Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle,” which set U.S. box office records for an anime feature.
	

	Hiroki Totoki, president and CEO of Sony Group Corp., will be on hand at the forum to deliver remarks, as will Ravi Ahuja, chairman and CEO of Sony Pictures Entertainment. The event will conclude with observations and news delivered by Rahul Purini, Crunchyroll president.

	New York Comic Con runs Oct. 8-10 at the Javits Center.

	(Pictured: Crunchyroll’s Rahul Purini and Mitchel Berger at Variety’s screening of “Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle” in November 2025.)

title: 49ers Owner Jed York Arrested in Ohio Prostitution-Related Case
description:
49ers Owner Jed York
                          Busted in Ohio Prostitution Case
body:
49ers Owner Jed York
                          Busted in Ohio Prostitution Case
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 24, 2026
                            8:20 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York landed in an Ohio jail Sunday ... after being arrested on suspicion of engaging in prostitution.
      
    
            York was busted in East Palestine and booked into the Columbiana County Jail before posting $5,000 bond.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The case moved quickly from there ... prosecutors amended the original engaging-in-prostitution count to misdemeanor disorderly conduct before York pleaded no contest Monday.
      
    
            York also pleaded no contest to possessing criminal tools -- a misdemeanor.
      

            A judge sentenced York to one day in jail on each count, served concurrently, with credit for time already served ... and ordered him to pay $1,150 in fines.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            According to WKBN, which first reported the news, York's cell phone was ordered returned to him ... while $160 seized in the case was forfeited to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force.
      
    
            York became 49ers team president in 2008 and is the franchise's majority owner.
      
    
            We've reached out to the 49ers for comment ... so far, no word back.

title: Sean Grayson Dies Months Into Sentence for Sonya Massey Killing
description:
Sean Grayson
                          Dies at 32, While in Prison for Sonya Massey Death
body:
Sean Grayson
                          Dies at 32, While in Prison for Sonya Massey Death
                          ... Suffered from Cancer
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 23, 2026
                            7:05 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 24, 2026
                                9:16 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Sean Grayson, the former Illinois sheriff's deputy convicted in the fatal shooting of Sonya Massey, has died.
      
    
            Grayson's attorney, Daniel Fultz, tells TMZ Sean died around noon Sunday Central Time. Fultz declined to provide any additional details. Sources close to the situation tell us the root cause of death was colon cancer.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Grayson was diagnosed with Stage 3 colon cancer in 2023. His attorneys later said the disease had progressed to Stage 4 and spread to his liver, lungs and rectum. In July, the Illinois Prisoner Review Board denied Grayson's request for medical release.
      

            Grayson was about six months into a 20-year sentence for second-degree murder ... after he was convicted in the 2024 shooting of Massey -- a 36-year-old woman who had called 911 to report a prowler at her Illinois home.
      
    
        
                    
                      7/6/24
                  
      
    
            The shooting happened shortly after deputies arrived at Massey's home and was captured on body camera video. The case sparked nationwide outrage, protests and calls for accountability.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            During his trial, Grayson testified that Massey picked up a pot of boiling water, causing him to back away. He said he believed she was going to throw it at him after she told him, "I rebuke you in the name of Jesus." Grayson said he interpreted the statement as a threat.

Hayden Panettiere's Mom
                          CLAIMS BF DRAINED HER & PAWNED HER STUFF
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 23, 2026
                            6:40 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 24, 2026
                                6:07 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Hayden Panettiere’s mom says Brian Hickerson left her daughter depleted in every way -- financially, emotionally and physically -- as he allegedly became deeply embedded in the actress’ life.
      
    
            Lesley Vogel -- Hayden's estranged mother -- says she came to L.A. about a year ago to help Hayden through a serious health struggle ... claiming Hayden was suffering from an unexplained pins-and-needles feeling in her lower body that made it difficult for her to walk or function normally, according to the The New York Times.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Hayden wondered whether the pain could have been connected to injuries she suffered while working as a child actor, and according to her mom, they sought help from doctors and tried massage and acupuncture in search of relief.
      

                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            Vogel also tells the outlet Hickerson allegedly pawned some of Hayden’s belongings -- including a vintage guitar -- and had other items in his storage unit.
      
    
            The two allegedly became even more intertwined when Hayden hired Hickerson as her assistant. His LinkedIn lists him as an executive assistant to a “high-profile confidential client,” with responsibilities including around-the-clock support, handling emails and caring for two dogs.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Vogel says her attempts to keep Hickerson out of Hayden’s finances and personal life contributed to a falling out with her daughter. Hayden had previously written that she sometimes felt intense pressure from her mom, who she felt could be more business manager than mother.
      
    
            As we previously reported … Hayden’s death remains under investigation, with local authorities, the coroner and DEA involved as toxicology results are pending.
      
    
            We also obtained docs showing Hickerson filed for bankruptcy in 2022, listing about $25,700 in assets and roughly $60,000 in debt.
